newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, but early losses pared.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, but early losses pared.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended weaker on Friday, but pared earlier losses as Wall Street finished the week on a strong note.
The TSE 300 Index slipped 9.20 points to close at 5817.36 in turnover of 84.9 million shares worth C$1.43 billion ($1.03 billion).
Declining stocks outpaced advances 511 to 372 with 311 issues unchanged.
"We pared our losses as New York turned their market turned around. We'll see if we can carry it on into next week," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose nearly 49 points to close around 6526 on Friday.
The TSE was hampered by weakness in other Canadian financial markets. Canadian bonds sagged along with a weaker Canadian dollar which hit a two-year low on Thursday.

An uexpectedly low March unemployment rate in Canada helped the currency on Friday, but analysts said the unit will remain under pressure until the Bank of Canada raises interest rates to match a recent rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
In Toronto, 11 of 14 sub-groups ended the day with moderate losses. The three strong sectors were consumer products, industrial products and real estate.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. finished its first complete session on the TSE since last week's stunning revelations that the Busang gold discovery may only contain small amounts of gold.
The Calgary-based gold prospector closed down 0.25 at 3.18 and led active issues with turnover of 8.0 million shares.
* Among other heavy traders, Bank of Nova Scotia fell 0.35 to 50.85 on 2.3 million shares. Royal Bank of Canada dipped 0.15 to 53.95 on 1.4 million shares.
Analysts said Canadian bank profits are expected to be hurt by rising U.S. interest rates which have dampened equity markets and the banks' key brokerage businesses.
